title: Policy telemetry and claim attenuation for cross-region operator roles
author: Claire Nguyen
description: Summary: Add policy-level telemetry counters and a claim-attenuation layer to reduce operator-scope creep across regions while preserving auditability. Motivation: We observed several incidents where broad operator claims from third-party operator services were being used to escalate cross-tenant reads in edge regions. This PR implements a low-risk attenuation shim plus telemetry to detect and gradually enforce narrower operator scopes. Design: 1) claim-attenuator service (policy/attenuator) that rewrites operator claims at the ingress point based on tenant residency, role templates and a configurable attenuation matrix; 2) policy telemetry (policy/telemetry) that emits rbac.enforced_decisions, rbac.attenuation_applied, and residency.assertion_mismatch metrics with tenant, region, and route tags; 3) audit enrichment that attaches attenuation_reason and original_claim_hash to existing audit envelopes (ops/audit/enricher) so post-hoc forensics can reconstruct decisions without exposing raw claims; 4) feature-flag driven rollout (ops/ff) enabling attenuation in detection mode (no deny) -> partial enforcement (10% tenants) -> full enforcement. Backwards compatibility: Attenuator defaults to 'observe' mode and does not drop or deny requests until explicit rollout; audit enrichment uses opt-in header X-Attenuation-Version to preserve older audit parsers. Rollout Plan: 1) deploy detection telemetry to staging and run for 72h; 2) enable partial enforcement for a small tenant cohort for 7d; 3) expand to 25% then 100% after operational sign-off. Testing: unit tests for rule resolution, integration tests cover policy decision logs, synthetic load test shows <3% median latency impact on auth path at 95th percentile. Operational controls: new console charts for rbac.enforced_decisions and attenuation_error_rate, an alert on attenuation_error_rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m, and a runbook for disabling attenuation per region. Security notes: attenuation rules are validated against legacy role templates to avoid unintended privilege escalation. Implementation notes: claim hashes are HMAC'd with KMS-derived key but not stored in plaintext. See commits and files changed for details.

comments: Miguel Santos (reviewer): Can we make the attenuation matrix configurable per-customer from the console? If not, we should add an RFC for that next sprint.

Author (Claire Nguyen): The initial rollout keeps the matrix static in cluster config; adding per-tenant configuration is tracked under ENG-3260. We intentionally avoided per-tenant writes in this PR to reduce blast radius.
Ravi Patel (reviewer): Audit envelope now contains claim_hash — ensure we don't violate PII/secret policies. Who reviewed KMS usage?

Author (Claire Nguyen): KMS usage was reviewed by security during design. claim_hash is HMAC with a KMS-derived key and we never persist raw claim data. See infra/kms/README.md for key rotation notes.
